direction.description: Direction in which the message is used, from the API's point of view (e.g. in means a message sent from the client to the API)

headerRef.description: Reference to a group header element, which can be a simple field containing the number of repeating group instances, or a component or group providing additional information about the group instance

typeRef.description: Reference to the data type of the element

type.description: The type of this data type, such as primitive, derived, array, composite, etc.

byteLength.description: Byte size of this data type, if it's of fixed length

terminatingChar.description: Character used to signify the end of the actual value of the field, for example \0 for null-terminated strings

paddingChar.description: Character used to pad the value, when the value is shorter than the field's length

paddingSide.description: Whether the padding character is added left of (before) or right of (after) the value

charSet.description: Default character set used for text data types, e.g. ASCII, UTF-8, etc.

dataTypeEncodings.description: List of encoding-specific data types into which this data type is encoded

derivedDataType.description: Data type derived from a base type

baseTypeRef.description: The base primitive type of this derived type

valuesTypeRef.description: The data type of the values of this enumerated type

values.description: List of allowed values if this data type is an enum

enumValue.description: Definition of a single valid value in a data type

value.description: The actual value of the field

category.description: Custom category name or grouping of this value

arrayDataType.description: Array data type representing a collection of elements of the same type

elementsTypeRef.description: The data type of elements in this array type

elementsUnique.description: Whether all elements in this array need to be unique or there can be duplicates

elementsOrdered.description: Whether the order of elements in this array is important

compositeDataType.description: Composite data type containing member elements

content.description: Child members of this composite data type

compositeDataTypeMember.description: Definition of a single member in a composite data type

typeRef.description: Reference to the data type of the member

presence.description: Presence requirement (e.g. required, optional, etc.) for this member in the parent composite data type

value.description: Default or constant value of this member (can be a string or a reference to an enum value)

bitsetDataType.description: A data type that uses single bits to encode information, usually each bit is a Boolean flag. Multi-bit ranges within the bitset are supported too.

bitLength.description: Total bit size of this data type (sum of all bitfield lengths)

content.description: Child members of this bitset data type

bitsetMember.description: Single bit or range in a bitset data type

bitOffset.description: The position of the bit (starting from 0). By default, the position and bit length of elements determines their offset. This property is usually explicitly specified only for sparse bitsets.

bitLength.description: Length in bits. Defaults to 1 for single-bit flags.

values.description: List of supported integer values (for multi-bit ranges)

bitsetMemberValue.description: Definition of a single valid value in a bitset data type

value.description: The actual value of the field

dataTypeEncoding.description: Definition of an encoding-specific data type

encoding.description: Name of encoding, e.g. tag-value, JSON, SBE, etc.

typeName.description: Name of data type in the specified encoding

valuePattern.description: Regex describing acceptable patterns for the value of this field

byteLength.description: Byte size of this data type, if it's of fixed length

terminatingChar.description: Character used to signify the end of the actual value of the field, for example \0 for null-terminated strings

paddingChar.description: Character used to pad the value, when the value is shorter than the field's length

paddingSide.description: Whether the padding character is added left of (before) or right of (after) the value

variant.description: Variant (different forms of the same element used for different use-cases) definition

changeLogEntry.description: Description of a single change to an element

changeType.description: The type of change made to the element

version.description: The version of the API that this change applies to

changeScope.description: Whether the change affects the API structure or if it's just an editorial change

replacedBy.description: If this is a replacement or deprecation, the element to use in place of this one

timestamp.description: The date and time when the change was made

trackingReference.description: External tracking reference (e.g. ticket ID or URL) related to this change

changeLog.description: List of changes to an element

documentationEntry.description: A single documentation entry for an element

role.description: The role of this documentation entry, such as summary, explanation, example, etc.

contentType.description: The MIME content type of the documentation text, e.g. text/plain, text/markdown, text/html, etc.

language.description: RFC 1766 language tag of the language used for the documentation text, e.g. en-us, ja, etc.

documentation.description: List of documentation entries for an element

additionalDataEntry.description: A single additional data entry for an element

role.description: The role of this additional data entry

additionalData.description: List of additional data entries (used to define custom, implementation-specific data and mappings) for an element

complexElement.description: Definition of a complex element (contains child elements, i.e. references to other elements), which can have variants

content.description: Child elements (references to other element definitions) of this complex element

contentComposition.description: Composition type of child elements (allOf - all required child elements must be present and optional child elements may be present, oneOf - exactly one child element must be present)

contentOrdering.description: Whether child elements must be in the defined order

simpleElement.description: Definition of a simple element (doesn't contain any child elements), which can have variants

category.description: Category that this element belongs to

id.description: A protocol-specific identifier of this element. For example, for the FIX protocol, this can be used to store field tags.

shortName.description: Short, abbreviated name of this element

childElement.description: Child element (reference to an element definition) within a complex element

refName.description: If a different name (compared to the element definition's name) should be used for this reference

presence.description: Presence requirement (e.g. required, optional, etc.) for this child element in the parent complex element

offset.description: Byte offset of this element in the message. Applicable to binary protocols

paddedLength.description: The total, fixed length of the element, including any necessary padding. This can be useful in binary protocols if variable-length content should always be padded to a fixed length.

elementReference.description: Reference to an element definition. It must use the same properties as the primary key defined for the type of element that's being referenced. Additional properties, in addition to the general ones specified below, can be used.

id.description: Protocol-specific identifier of the referenced element

elementAnnotation.description: Auxiliary information (such as documentation, additional data, and change log) for an element

fieldProperties.description: Common properties for field definitions and references

value.description: Default or constant value of this field (can be a string or a reference to an enum value)

lengthHeaderRef.description: Reference to another element specifying the length of this field

valueQualifierRef.description: Reference to another field that qualifies and provides context for interpreting the value of this field. For example, for a Symbol field, the value qualifier will be another field that specifies what instrument identifier (ISIN, RIC, BBG, etc.) is used.

allowOtherValues.description: If the field has a data type containing enumerated values, this property denotes whether additional values, not defined in the data type, are acceptable

valuePattern.description: Regex describing acceptable patterns for the value of this field

minLength.description: Minimum allowed length (inclusive) of the value of this field. Generally used for length of a string field or number of elements in an array.

maxLength.description: Maximum allowed length (inclusive) of the value of this field. Generally used for length of a string field or number of elements in an array.

byteLength.description: Byte size of the value of this field. Overrides the value defined in the field's data type

charSet.description: Character set used for text field, e.g. ASCII, UTF-8, etc. Overrides the value defined in the field's data type

terminatingChar.description: Character used to signify the end of the actual value of the field, for example \0 for null-terminated strings. Overrides the value defined in the data type

paddingChar.description: Character used to pad the value, when the value is shorter than the field's length. Overrides the value defined in the data type.

paddingSide.description: Whether the padding character is added left of (before) or right of (after) the value. Overrides the value defined in the data type.

groupProperties.description: Common properties for group definitions and references

minInstances.description: Minimum allowed number of instances (inclusive) of this repeating group

maxInstances.description: Maximum allowed number of instances (inclusive) of this repeating group

keyPropertiesList.description: List of properties used as a unique key for an element

keysDefinition.description: Definition of unique keys for a specific type of elements

primaryKey.description: Primary unique key used to identify and reference an element

alternateKeys.description: Alternate keys used as additional uniqueness constraints

section.description: Section that this category belongs to

id.description: Identifier (e.g. UUID, URL, etc.) of the API

url.description: External link to the page or additional description of the API

protocolVersion.description: Protocol-specific version (e.g. FIX version) of the API

endianness.description: Whether data is encoded in big or little endian format (applicable to binary APIs)

keys.description: Keys define uniqueness constraints for different types of elements. For example, if the key for fields is "name", that means that there cannot be two fields with the same name. A key can contain one or more element attributes. The primary key is used for referencing elements from other elements. Alternate keys are additional uniqueness constraints, which are not used for referencing. If the primary key for some type is omitted, it will default to "name" and "variant". There are no alternate keys by default. An exception are enumerated values in data types, which use just "name" as the default primary key, and have "value" as a default alternate key.

messages.description: Definition of unique keys for messages. If omitted, defaults to "name" and "variant" as the primary key, and no alternate keys.

components.description: Definition of unique keys for components. If omitted, defaults to "name" and "variant" as the primary key, and no alternate keys.

groups.description: Definition of unique keys for groups. If omitted, defaults to "name" and "variant" as the primary key, and no alternate keys.

fields.description: Definition of unique keys for fields. If omitted, defaults to "name" and "variant" as the primary key, and no alternate keys.

dataTypes.description: Definition of unique keys for data types. If omitted, defaults to "name" and "variant" as the primary key, and no alternate keys.

values.description: Definition of unique keys for enumerated values of data types. If omitted, defaults to "name" as the primary key, and "value" as the alternate key.

messages.description: List of messages defined in the API

components.description: List of components defined in the API

groups.description: List of groups defined in the API

fields.description: List of fields defined in the API

dataTypes.description: List of data types defined in the API

variants.description: List of variants (different forms of the same element used for different use-cases) defined in the API

categories.description: List of categories (grouping for elements) defined in the API

sections.description: List of sections (grouping for categories) defined in the API
